articles.title: ‘South Park’ Creators Apologize for the Years-Long Delay of Their Kendrick Lamar Movie: ‘We Still Believe in the Project’
articles.summary: “South Park” co-creators Trey Parker and Matt Stone have released an official apology for delaying their mysterious film collaboration with Kendrick Lamar. “We take full responsibility for the schedule delay of this movie,” Parker and Stone said in a statement to The Ankler.
body: The musical comedy movie, operating under the working title “Whitney Springs,” is in production at Paramount, which is also the home of “South Park.” Parker and Stone are working on the project under their Park County banner. Lamar is also producing alongside Dave Free and his pgLang company.

Early loglines stated that “Whitney Springs” follows a Black man working as a slave reenactor at a living history museum who discovers his white girlfriend’s family once owned his ancestors. The Ankler reported a slight variation on the story. The outlet claims that the film follows the Black slave reenactor as he clashes with the racist mayor of a Midwestern town, who will be played by Parker. Lamar, The Ankler said, has recorded several original songs for the project.

articles.title: Trump White House Pulls Down Tetris-Like Game, in Which You Had to Stop a ‘Zombie Siege’ at Mexican Border, After Company’s Copyright Threat
articles.summary: The White House has removed the “Build the Wall” game — a Tetris knockoff in which players were tasked with fortifying the southern U.S. border to keep out illegal immigrants — after the company that owns the rights to the popular title issued a statement saying it “take[s] copyright infringement…
body: Reps for the White House and the Tetris Company did not respond to requests for comment.

Tetris Holding LLC is the owner of Tetris rights worldwide, and the Tetris Company is its exclusive licensee. In a statement posted to social media Friday, the Tetris Company said: “At Tetris we believe in the power of connection and bringing people together, not dividing them. To our fans everywhere: we love you, we see you, and we’re grateful to have you in our community.”

The company also noted it “was not involved in the creation of ‘Build the Wall.’” When asked whether the Tetris Company was considering taking legal action with respect to the White House’s game, a rep last Friday said the company was “reviewing the matter.”

Meanwhile, as of Wednesday afternoon, another anti-immigration game called “Rio Run,” which is patterned on the classic snake video-game genre, was still available on the White House game site. In that game, users “patrol the line” along the Rio Grande and collect illegal immigrants in a long chain behind a white officer in order to expel them from the U.S.

articles.title: ‘The Fire Within You’ Review: An Insufferable Christmas Eve Family Drama in Which the Corrosive Rants Are as Noxious as the Dyspeptic Images
articles.summary: Let’s hope there was a giant extractor fan on the set of “The Fire Within You,” because the stench of burnt oil must have been overwhelming. It’s not only food that gets blistered in Edoardo De Angelis’ overwrought screaming match, which makes one envious of the wax Odysseus had handy to plug up…
body: A mother from hell teeters around with a glass in hand pouring bile on everyone in reach, but because she’s the “mamma,” Eduardo De Angelis mistakenly believes she deserves our sympathy.

Her cooking is as poisonous as her words, yet both gush out in a non-stop flow of over-fried eggplant, aggressively hacked cod and salad drowning in oil. With the arrival of Angela’s daughter Paola (Ivana Lotito), the nastiness increases — at least Paola has the ability to talk back, unlike Antonio, who keeps taking abuse, such as “it would have been better if you had died at birth,” until he finally explodes, accompanied by a burst of shattered glass.

articles.title: Russian director refuses to denounce lead actor despite criticism from Ukraine
articles.summary: Ilya Khrzhanovsky’s DAU, about physicist Lev Landau, stars Russian conductor Teodor Currentzis, who has refused to speak out against Putin’s war. The director of a controversial new Russian film has said “everyone pays for his own choice” when asked about his lead’s refusal to condemn Russia’s war…
body: In film-maker Ilya Khrzhanovsky’s DAU, which premiered at the Venice film festival on Wednesday, Greek-Russian star conductor Teodor Currentzis plays the eponymously nicknamed protagonist, Nobel prize-winning quantum physicist Lev Landau.

In the run-up to the festival, the film’s inclusion in the lineup was heavily criticised by the Ukrainian ministry of foreign affairs, in part over the fact that Athens-born Currentzis continues to live and work in Russia, and has never publicly denounced Putin’s war.

“It’s his choice,” Khrzhanovsky said at a press conference on the Lido. “But I think everyone is paying for his own choice, his own life, his own destiny,” added the film-maker, who has renounced his Russian citizenship over the full-scale invasion and lives in exile in Germany.

He referred to his film, in which Currentzis’s character Landau is put under pressure to work on the development of the nuclear bomb and eventually reluctantly agrees. “As you can see in the movie, the main character is also making different choices, and he’s paying for his choices.”

articles.title: Billy Joel Says He Had Brain Surgery After His Diagnosis: ‘Don’t Worry About Me’
articles.summary: Billy Joel says he is doing better after brain surgery helped relieve some of the symptoms of normal pressure hydrocephalus, a disorder he was diagnosed with in 2025. On SiriusXM’s Billy Joel channel Wednesday, the singer talked about the surgery he agreed to after noticing “my balance was not…
body: His neurologist said that since it was possible it could continue to get worse, he recommended that Joel have a shunt implanted in his brain. Joel said on Sirius that although he initially didn’t want to have a hole drilled through his brain, after researching it he realized it could help with balance and help memory.
“I don’t want to lose my marbles,” he said. “It’s hard to tell what’s your age and what’s a condition.

“So they implanted a shunt in my brain and it actually improved things. My memory got better, my balance got a little better, my ability to function was better. I realized that because of my job, which is playing rock and roll music very loud, that it was giving me something like a concussion every time I did a show.”
“I’m ok. I want people to know, don’t worry about me. I’m still here,” he assured fans on Wednesday.

articles.title: Union Town review – passionate exposé of US delivery workers’ employment conditions
articles.summary: Venice film festival: Barbara Kopple returns with her third film investigating US workers’ rights – this time, undocumented ‘deliveristas’ and the attempts to unionise Amazon staff.
body: Barbara Kopple’s documentary about app-based delivery workers is a stirring, defiant, battle-hardened affair, swinging between the fraught picket line and the still more hazardous New York City streets. It’s a new film that feels old in the best sense of the word; a hoarse battle cry that summons the ghosts of The Grapes of Wrath and the New Deal, Eugene Debs and Woody Guthrie. That America is long dead and buried, a casualty of changing times, but Kopple sees no reason why it should not rise again.

articles.title: John Malkovich cancels Israel trip over fabricated solidarity quote
articles.summary: The Wild Horse Nine actor had been due to appear on stage in The Music Critic in Tel Aviv – but pulled out over PR firm’s ‘unacceptable and untenable’ attribution of statement.
body: John Malkovich has cancelled a planned trip to Israel next year to appear on stage after a PR firm hired by the show attributed quotes to the actor that the company had written.

Malkovich, who is a leading Oscar contender for his role in Martin McDonagh’s Wild Horse Nine, was due to appear in The Music Critic, a theatrical-musical satire composed by the Jewish violinist Aleksey Igudesman, in Tel Aviv’s Charles Bronfman Auditorium on 13 April.

A press release circulated on 5 September quoted Malkovich as saying he was “thrilled to return to Israel” and looked “forward to meeting the warm Israeli audience once again, to whom I feel a strong closeness and solidarity”.

The actor, 72, was alerted to the quotes after reading them in the Hollywood Reporter, who picked them up from the Jerusalem Post. In a statement to the Hollywood Reporter on 8 September, Malkovich said that a “PR company hired by the Israeli promoter drafted a quote for the article that was attributed to me, though I never made the statements that were quoted, nor was I consulted before they were printed.”

articles.title: BBC drops Drag Race UK after eight series
articles.summary: Future series will no longer be broadcast on BBC Three as the show moves to a streaming platform owned by its production company.
body: RuPaul's Drag Race UK is leaving the BBC after eight series, the broadcaster has confirmed.
A spokesperson for the channel said it was facing "very difficult choices" in the face of "significant financial pressures".

The show is currently broadcast on BBC Three and iPlayer. Future series - as well as its spin-off vs The World - will be broadcast on Wow Presents Plus, a streaming platform owned by the production company behind the show.
At its peak, the UK version of the international drag competition averaged at around 1.5 million viewers per episode.

articles.title: The Uprising review – the peasants are revolting in muddled historical epic
articles.summary: Andrew Garfield’s charisma can’t save Paul Greengrass’s grim and depressingly generic period piece. Hollywood loves giving young actors their own historical epic as much as audiences seem to dislike watching them.
body: On paper, The Uprising should be different: it’s a historical epic from a blue-chip director (the Bourne trilogy’s Paul Greengrass ), a nuanced, introspective leading man ( Andrew Garfield ) and a milieu that uncomfortably chimes with the western world’s backslide into repressive authoritarianism (The Peasants’ Revolt of 1381). In reality, it is a disjointed slog through the mud with the emotional depth of a History Channel rerun.

Thus follows a rather hectic-feeling race from one greige setting to the next as the rebels have their run of modern-day Kent, assembling in Maidstone before storming Canterbury cathedral, and then traveling to meet the king and his men in Blackheath. Greengrass’s camerawork can occasionally swoon, with stunning aerial shots of a flotilla on the Thames, but his signature handheld style is a trick that has gone stale: the only uprising I felt during the seasick fight scenes was my breakfast threatening to return on me.
points: Andrew Garfield’s charisma can’t save Paul Greengrass’s grim and depressingly generic period piece.
Hollywood loves giving young actors their own historical epic as much as audiences seem to dislike watching them.

articles.title: Barry Melrose, Entertaining ESPN Hockey Analyst, Dies at 70
articles.summary: After 11 pro seasons as a rugged player, he led the L.A. Kings to the Stanley Cup Final in his first season as an NHL coach, then handled colorful commentary from 1994-2022.
body: Barry Melrose, the blue-collar NHL defenseman who brought flash to the Los Angeles Kings as their coach and fun to ESPN during his nearly three decades as a colorful hockey analyst, has died. He was 70.

“A rangy and rugged defenseman from Kelvington, Saskatchewan, Barry fashioned an 11-year pro career in the NHL, AHL and WHA. But it was as a coach, who guided the Los Angeles Kings to the 1993 Stanley Cup Final, and as a broadcaster, who spent 27 years at ESPN, that he truly made his mark upon the game. And during those countless encounters over the years with players, coaches, fans and viewers who couldn’t help but be drawn in by his enthusiasm.

“We mourn the passing of a hockey original. And we send our deepest condolences to his wife, Cindy, their sons, Tyrell and Adrien, and all of his teammates, colleagues and admirers around the hockey world,” Bettman concluded.
Melrose’s cause of death wasn’t immediately available. In October 2023, he revealed that he had been diagnosed with Parkinson’s disease and was retiring.

articles.title: ‘South Park’ Creators Apologize to Kendrick Lamar, Paramount for Movie’s Delay: “We Still Believe in the Project”
articles.summary: Trey Parker and Matt Stone have been working with Lamar on the musical comedy known as 'Whitney Springs,' which has been shrouded in mystery and had its release date delayed multiple times.
body: Hope may still spring eternal for fans of South Park creators Trey Parker and Matt Stone amid a new update surrounding the movie that they have been working on with Kendrick Lamar.

“We take full responsibility for the schedule delay of this movie,” Parker and Stone said in the new statement. “We apologize to our partners at pgLang and Paramount, and we appreciate their patience. South Park and life’s circumstances have gotten in the way, but we still believe in the project.”

According to The Ankler, the film’s plot centers on a Black reenactor at a historical slave plantation museum who clashes with the Midwest town’s racist mayor, played by Parker. The outlet reports that the movie includes original, unreleased songs from Grammy Award-winning rapper Lamar.

The Hollywood Reporter reported in November that Whitney Springs would no longer hit theaters on its planned release date of March 20, 2026, as the film was pulled from the calendar. Previously, the film had been shifted from its initial release date of July 4, 2025, amid Lamar’s forthcoming tour and South Park production responsibilities.
